chunks.text: OCT4, SOX2, KLF4, and c-MYC first reprogrammed human somatic cells to pluripotency. Unlike in mouse, OCT4 substitution in human cells previously failed, but transcriptome/bioinformatic analysis identified lineage-specifier factors replacing OCT4 and SOX2 in human fibroblasts, supporting counteracting lineage-specification networks. HDAC inhibitor valproic acid boosted reprogramming efficiency over 100-fold (Oct4-GFP reporter) and enabled pluripotent stem cell induction without c-Myc. G-quadruplex (G4)-forming sequences, including telomeres, act as replication fork barriers; homologous recombination stabilizes/restarts stalled forks. G-rich telomeric repeat replication efficiency dropped significantly in HR-lacking cells, and G4-stabilizer pyridostatin increased telomere fragility in BRCA2-deficient cells, reducing proliferation via double-strand breaks, checkpoint activation, and deregulated G2/M—including olaparib-resistant cells (53BP1/REV7 loss). Psoralen-induced interstrand cross-links caused chromosome breakage and 4N delay only after S-phase; primary human fibroblasts removed ~2,500 ICLs/genome at ~11 ICLs/genome/h.

Three studies report mouse genetic models. mGluR6 knockout mice, exploiting the receptor's restricted expression in retinal ON bipolar cells, lost ON responses to light while OFF responses remained unchanged; retinal organization and optic fiber projections to the brain were normal, and mutant mice still showed visual behavioral responses in shuttle box avoidance experiments, indicating mGluR6 is essential for synaptic transmission to ON bipolar cells and the OFF pathway carries important visual information. A conditional p75(NTR) allele (p75(NTR-FX)) flanking Exons 4-6, encoding transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains, with loxP sites was validated via neural crest-specific p75(NTR)/Wnt1-Cre and conventional null mutants, both showing abnormal hind limb reflexes and peripheral neuropathy. Nrg1 and ErbB4 signalling cell-autonomously controls development of cortical GABA interneuron connectivity, contradicting the prevailing excitatory-synapse view.

Three papers: (1) FASEB J 2001 (10.1096/fj.00-0815fje) reports cholesterol's essential role in synaptic plasticity and neuronal degeneration: cholesterol efflux induced ex vivo by human CSF-HDL3 and methyl-β-cyclodextrin impairs short- and long-term plasticity in adult rat hippocampal slices (CA1 fEPSPs, immunofluorescence). (2) ATM deficiency causes nuclear HDAC4 accumulation in neurons, promoting ataxia-telangiectasia neurodegeneration; nuclear HDAC4 binds chromatin, MEF2A and CREB, altering gene expression. Blocking HDAC4 activity or nuclear accumulation rescues ATM-deficient mouse behaviors, though full rescue needs cytoplasmic HDAC4; ATM phosphorylation downregulates PP2A, whose excess activity dephosphorylates HDAC4. (3) Osteoblast-secreted PGE2 activates sensory-nerve EP4, inhibiting sympathetic activity via the CNS to regulate bone formation; PGE2 rises as bone density falls in osteoporotic models; sensory nerve ablation erodes skeletal integrity.

# Detection and distribution patterns of telomerase activity in insects.

Telomeres of most insects consist of pentanucleotide (TTAGG)n repeats, although the repeats are absent in Diptera and some other insect species, where the telomere regions are perhaps maintained without telomerase. To understand various and unusual telomere formation in insects, we have studied the characteristic features of a putative insect telomerase that has not been previously described. Using a modified telomeric repeat amplification protocol (TRAP), we first detected the telomerase activity in crickets, cockroaches and two Lepidopteran insects. The telomerase from crickets and cockroaches required dATP, dGTP and dTTP but not dCTP as a substrate and sequence analyses of the products of TRAP revealed that the (TTAGG)n repeats are synthesized by telomerase. The cockroach telomerase was detected both in somatic (fat body, muscle and neural tissues) and germ line (testis) cells, suggesting that expression of this enzyme is not regulated in a tissue-specific manner at an adult stage. While we detected high levels of telomerase activity in crickets and cockroaches, we could not detect activity in all tissues and cell cultures of the silkworm, Bombyx mori and in two Drosophila and one Sarcophaga cell lines. This supports the theory that Dipteran insects maintain their telomeres without telomerase.

Two studies show non-coding 3'UTRs modulate microRNA function. In mouse breast carcinoma 4T1 cells, the versican 3'UTR antagonizes miR-199a-3p, lowering its levels; miR-199a-3p and miR-144 target cell-cycle regulator Rb1, while miR-144 and miR-136 target PTEN. By binding these miRNAs, the 3'UTR freed Rb1 and PTEN mRNAs for translation, up-regulating both synergistically in vitro and in vivo. Cells transfected with the 3'UTR formed smaller tumors than controls, implicating miRNA degradation in tumorigenesis. Separately, the ~1.7 kb spliced, highly abundant murine cytomegalovirus m169 transcript mediates rapid, mutual degradation of cellular miR-27a/b during lytic infection via a single optimized miRNA binding site in its 3'-UTR. Expressing only the m169 3'-UTR from an adenoviral vector sufficed; degradation involved 3'-tailing and trimming. Three mutant viruses unable to target miR-27a/b lost efficiency in vivo.

Two studies show non-coding 3'UTRs modulate microRNA function. Versican 3'UTR antagonizes and lowers miR-199a-3p levels in mouse breast carcinoma 4T1 cells; miR-199a-3p and miR-144 target cell-cycle regulator Rb1, while miR-144 and miR-136 target PTEN. The 3'UTR bound these miRNAs, freeing Rb1 and PTEN mRNAs for translation, up-regulating them synergistically in vitro and in vivo. Cells transfected with the 3'UTR formed smaller tumors than controls, implicating miRNA degradation in tumorigenesis. Separately, the ~1.7 kb spliced, highly abundant murine cytomegalovirus m169 transcript mediates rapid degradation of cellular miR-27a/b during lytic infection, via a single optimized miRNA binding site in its 3'-UTR. Expressing only the m169 3'-UTR from an adenoviral vector sufficed; degradation involved 3'-tailing and -trimming and was mutual. Three mutant viruses unable to target miR-27a/b lost efficiency in vivo.

# DNA replication is required To elicit cellular responses to psoralen-induced DNA interstrand cross-links.

Following introduction of DNA interstrand cross-links (ICLs), mammalian cells display chromosome breakage or cell cycle delay with a 4N DNA content. To further understand the nature of the delay, previously described as a G(2)/M arrest, we developed a protocol to generate ICLs during specific intervals of the cell cycle. Synchronous populations of G(1), S, and G(2) cells were treated with photoactivated 4'-hydroxymethyl-4,5',8-trimethylpsoralen (HMT) and scored for normal passage into mitosis. In contrast to what was found for ionizing radiation, ICLs introduced during G(2) did not result in a G(2)/M arrest, mitotic arrest, or chromosome breakage. Rather, subsequent passage through S phase was required to trigger both chromosome breakage and arrest in the next cell cycle. Similarly, ICLs introduced during G(1) did not cause a G(1)/S arrest. We conclude that DNA replication is required to elicit the cellular responses of cell cycle arrest and genomic instability after psoralen-induced ICLs. In primary human fibroblasts, the 4N DNA content cell cycle arrest triggered by ICLs was long lasting but reversible. Kinetic analysis suggested that these cells could remove up to approximately 2,500 ICLs/genome at an average rate of 11 ICLs/genome/h.

Simvastatin reduces CD40 expression in an experimental model of early arterialization of saphenous vein grafts (VG). Saphenous vein and internal mammary artery (IMA) samples from sixteen patients without statin therapy underwent pulsatile pressure distension and culture with or without Simvastatin (Merck Sharp & Dohme). CD40 was significantly lower in IMA than in distended and non-distended VG. Pressure distension upregulated CD40 in VG segments after 24 and 48 h. Simvastatin significantly reduced CD40 in both venous and arterial samples (P < 0.001 each); this effect was unaffected by L-NAME but reversed by mevalonic acid. Mean soluble CD40L (sCD40L) in culture supernatants increased over time, indicating the vessel wall—not only platelets—is a source of CD40/sCD40L. Simvastatin modulates endothelial CD40–sCD40L in venous and arterial grafts, suggesting a pharmacological tool to prevent graft failure.

Disruption of cell adhesion drives cancer dedifferentiation, invasion, and metastasis. Immunohistochemistry of desmoglein 1/2/3, desmocollin 2, integrin beta 4 (ITGB4), laminin gamma chain 2 (LAMC2), and collagen type 17 alpha 1 (COL17A1) was performed in 51 oral squamous cell carcinoma cases. In normal oral epithelium, DSG1, DSG3, DSC2, and COL17A1 localized to the plasma membrane, while ITGB4 and mature LAMC2 localized to the basement membrane. In cancer, DSG1, DSG3, DSC2, and COL17A1 decreased and internalized cytoplasmically; DSG2, ITGB4, and LAMC2 showed induced cytoplasmic expression in stroma-facing cells. Reduced DSG3 and DSC2 correlated with less differentiation, greater invasiveness, and higher nodal metastasis; lower COL17A1 and higher LAMC2 also indicated aggressive phenotype. Aberrant expression and localization of desmosomal and hemidesmosomal proteins therefore associate with aggressive clinicopathological features.

Mouse ES cell-derived clones and chimeras frequently show fetal growth abnormalities, producing over- or under-weight offspring with elevated neonatal mortality and morbidity. Since imprinted genes regulate fetal growth, improper epigenetic reprogramming of cultured cells is suspected. This study examined expression of two growth-regulatory imprinted genes, Igf2 and H19, in mouse ES cells grown under growth-restricted conditions and after in vitro aging. Serum-depleted media (starvation) and high cell density (confluence) increased expression of both genes and caused aberrant methylation profiles of differentially methylated regions at key regulatory sites of Igf2 and H19. These results confirm that growth-constrained culture alters methylation of imprinted gene regulatory domains and their expression patterns, suggesting epigenetic factors may contribute to the loss of developmental potential in ES cell-derived offspring.
